verses.text: After Jesus finished giving his twelve disciples these instructions, he headed out to teach and preach in their towns.
John was in prison when he heard what the Messiah was doing. He sent two of his disciples
to ask him, “Are you the One who’s coming, or should we expect somebody else?”
Jesus answered them, “Go tell John what you’re hearing and seeing:
“Blind people see again, people who couldn’t walk are walking, people with leprosy are cleansed, deaf people hear, the dead are raised, and the poor hear the Good News. 🙌
“Blessed is anyone who doesn’t trip over me.”
As John’s disciples headed off, Jesus began talking to the crowds about him: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see—a reed swaying in the wind?
“What did you go out there to see—a man dressed in soft clothes? Look, people wearing soft clothes live in royal houses.
“So why did you go? To see a prophet? Yes—and I’m telling you, he’s more than a prophet.
“He’s the one Scripture speaks about: ‘Look, I’m sending my messenger ahead of you; he’ll prepare your way.’
“I’m telling you the truth: among everyone born of women, nobody greater than John the Baptizer has appeared. Yet the least person in Heaven’s Kingdom is greater than he is.
“From the days of John the Baptizer until now, Heaven’s Kingdom has faced violence, and violent people are trying to seize it.
“All the prophets and the Law spoke ahead about what would happen up to John.
“And if you’re ready to accept it, he is Elijah, the one who was to come.
“If you’ve got ears, listen up.
“What can I compare this generation to? It’s like children sitting in the marketplaces, calling out to their friends:
“‘We played music for you, but you didn’t dance; we sang a funeral song, but you didn’t grieve.’
“John came without eating or drinking, and people said, ‘He has a demon.’
“The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Look at him—a glutton, a drunk, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ But wisdom is shown right by what it produces.”
Then Jesus began calling out the towns where he’d done most of his mighty works, because they still hadn’t turned back to God.
“How terrible for you, Chorazin! How terrible for you, Bethsaida! If the mighty works done among you had happened in Tyre and Sidon, they would’ve turned back long ago in rough cloth and ashes.
“But I’m telling you, judgment day will go easier for Tyre and Sidon than for you.
“And you, Capernaum—think you’ll be lifted all the way to heaven? You’ll go down to Hades. If the mighty works done in you had happened in Sodom, it would still be standing today.
“I’m telling you, judgment day will go easier for Sodom than for you.”
At that time Jesus said, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth: you’ve hidden these things from the wise and clever and shown them to little children.
“Yes, Father, because this was what pleased you.
“My Father has handed everything over to me. No one truly knows the Son except the Father, and no one truly knows the Father except the Son and anyone the Son chooses to reveal him to.
“Come to me, all of you worn out and carrying heavy loads, and I’ll give you rest. 🫶
“Take my yoke and learn from me. I’m gentle and humble in heart, and you’ll find rest for your souls.
“My yoke fits well, and my load is light.”
